answer: Both an Irish ICAV and an Irish investment company plc can be umbrella funds with legally segregated sub-funds; each sub-fund’s assets and liabilities are generally ring-fenced. **Accounts:** An ICAV may prepare sub-fund financial statements where its constitutional documents and applicable rules permit, but it must also prepare audited entity-level annual accounts. A plc generally prepares company-level statutory accounts; sub-fund reporting is commonly presented as additional sections/schedules, not separate statutory accounts. **AGMs:** An ICAV can elect in its constitution to dispense with AGMs, subject to statutory conditions and member rights. A plc is generally subject to company-law AGM requirements, though investment-company exceptions/dispensation may apply—check its status and documents. **US tax elections:** Neither form automatically qualifies for US “check-the-box” treatment. US classification/elections depend on entity eligibility, ownership and whether each sub-fund is treated as a separate entity; obtain US tax advice and confirm the exact structure with counsel.
